title: I Took the Observatory Public-Night Queue to the Intern Who Cut

parts.text: I took a number at 8:22 p.m. and the intern walked a friend straight to the eyepiece. The public-night card the intern handed out said: NUMBERED QUEUE. STAFF GUESTS WAIT TOO. I was forty-one, first visit, holding number 17 and a kid who had read the planet sheet twice. Intern Wes said, "Demo guests are curriculum." I pointed at the card. He shrugged. "Curriculum doesn't take a number." I photographed the friend at the eyepiece, the card, and number 17. Then I took the stills to the astronomer on duty. At 8:27 the astronomer asked why Wes's name was on a queue-cut ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The astronomer can see a staff guest at the eyepiece ahead of number 17.

social.video_title: The intern cut the public-night queue — Part 1/2
social.description: Number 17, a kid with a planet sheet, and a curriculum friend. I took the stills upstairs. Would you have skipped Saturn?

parts.text: Wes called it outreach until the kid asked for the number log. I printed the ticket, the card, and the photo. We got the eyepiece. Wes's friend took a number and told the dome the card was always about optics. Optics is a word interns use when Saturn is in a still. Queue policy now has a second line: CURRICULUM TAKES A NUMBER. I keep 17 as a joke. Wes hands cards he follows. The dome finally turns for the line.

social.description: Cut ticket, a real look at Saturn, and a second line on the card. Was outreach ever a skip?
